_comment: Gate ③ (scripts/gates/public-boundary.mjs) scans every git-tracked file's content against the regex patterns below. Any match fails the gate. This table is DATA, not code, on purpose — what counts as 'private' is repo-specific, and you are expected to edit this file for your own registry. Prefer regex over literal samples: a literal 'user:pass@host'-shaped example is itself flagged by secretlint elsewhere in this platform, and the same logic applies here — describe the SHAPE of what's forbidden, don't paste a shaped-like-real instance of it.
_bootstrap: ★ FIRST THING AFTER `agentdock init`: fill in `hostPrivateIdentifiers` below. It ships EMPTY on purpose — a template cannot know your host project's name, and a wrong guess is worse than an honest blank. This was measured, not assumed: a dry run of this gate over 14 real skills extracted from a private monorepo caught the host's source path but MISSED three sibling references to the same host by product name (a `~/.<product>/` runtime dir, a `$<PRODUCT>_SKILLS_ROOT` env var, and a `Library/Application Support/<Product>` path). The single highest-value pattern in this whole file is your own product name, and only you can supply it.

hostPrivateIdentifiers.description: 本仓的宿主私有标识：thefoolai 私有 monorepo 的仓名/产品名/源路径。注意 CogitoTech 这个 GitHub org 不在此列——agentdock 是公开仓，README 里指向它的出处署名是有意为之，把 org 名列为私有标识是误报（本仓 day one 就踩过一次，按门的规矩收窄了正则而不是加忽略名单）。

hostRuntimePaths.description: Paths and env vars that couple a skill to one host application's runtime. A portable skill should never reference where a specific app stores its data — if one of these matches, the skill is host-coupled and needs genericizing before it is published (this category is generic on purpose; the host-SPECIFIC names go in hostPrivateIdentifiers above).

privateRepoPaths.description: Filesystem paths or repo names that only make sense inside a private host repo. Defaults below catch generic 'private/internal' path segments only — your host's actual app/repo paths belong in hostPrivateIdentifiers, not here (shipping one consumer's private path as a generic default is how a template ends up carrying someone else's secrets).

internalDomains.description: Hostnames that only resolve on a private network, or internal-use subdomains. Defaults below catch RFC1918 IPv4 ranges, .internal/.local TLDs, and a generic 'internal.' subdomain prefix. Add your own org's non-public hostnames here.

personallyIdentifiable.description: Patterns shaped like real personal data. Defaults below catch Chinese mainland mobile numbers and 18-digit resident ID numbers by shape (not a specific real one). This category is the one most likely to need per-repo additions (e.g. a regex for how your team's git author names/emails appear) — the incident that motivated this gate was a half-redacted surname, not something a generic pattern alone would have caught, so treat these defaults as a floor, not a ceiling.
